messages:
morgan: Quick question — we're planning to rotate weight variants (fp16 -> q4 -> q4_0.5) without dropping traffic. What's the minimal atomic activation & TTL gating plan?

sasha: TL;DR: content-addressed bundle + activate manifest + lease TTL on nodes. Activation = rename manifest. :thinking:

tonY: rename across mounts isn't atomic; need control-plane coordinated activation or node-local symlink swap.

morgan: Right. Concern: writers during activation -> readers must tolerate transient missing files. Options: hardlink+rename of bundle dir then symlink switch.

sasha: We had a "hot-swap directory" pattern in the RFC but didn't finalize. My proposal: upload bundle -> verify checksum -> place in /var/weights/ready/<hash>/ -> publish atomic activation by updating control-plane manifest pointer. Nodes watch manifest and swap when validated.

emily: Restarting the loader isn't acceptable for low-latency. Loader should support live pointer update (inotify or polling) and ephemeral handle swap without restart.

tonY: Loader-level swap requires either RCU-like pointer switch or versioned manifest readers. RCU is simpler: keep an in-memory pointer to active manifest, swap it once validation passes. Readers see old pointer until swap is done.

morgan: And what about in-flight KV cache? We need per-request prefix cache invalidation on variant change to avoid serving mismatched activations.

sasha: Proposal: TTL gating + warmup metrics. Assign activation lease with TTL (e.g., 60s). A node accepts a variant only after warmup metric passes (prefetch hit rate >= threshold) or TTL expiry triggers fallback to previous variant.

morgan: Can we express warmup policy in compact config? Example config:

```json
{
  "warmup":{
    "min_prefetch_hits":0.6,
    "probe_samples":100,
    "ttl_seconds":60
  }
}
```

emily: That looks fine. Also add an explicit "graceful_fallback": "previous_variant_hash" field so node knows rollback target.

tonY: Rollout plan idea: 1% canary -> sample traffic to new variant via routing policy -> metrics to watch: p99 latency, tokens/s, failure-rate, and sample-quality (eval harness). Revert automatically on threshold exceed.

devbot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for variant 9f3c... on 3 hosts :rocket:

sasha: Storage note: prefer immutable, content-addressed bundles so GC and dedupe are trivial. Use a manifest that maps layer -> file path + checksum. Eg manifest snippet: 

```json
{
  "manifest_version": "1",
  "layers": [
    {"name":"w0", "path":"bundles/9f3c/layer0.safetensors", "sha256": "..."}
  ]
}
```

morgan: One more question: online transcode (fp16->q4) — do we transcode at upload or lazily on node? Tradeoff: upload CPU vs node storage + first-request latency.

emily: Prefer upload-time transcode to produce ready-to-serve variants. For rare variants, support lazy transcode as async background job and keep a CPU fallback path until ready.

sasha: Agreed. Upload-time transcode simplifies warmup and prevents per-request stalls. Lazy transcode ok as an escape hatch.

morgan: Ok. Can someone proto the minimal manifest + loader API with explicit activation/lease endpoints? @tony?

tonY: I'll sketch a tiny follow-up RFC and ping ops. ETA EOD. :thumbsup:

morgan: Great, thanks. Keeping this thread as the follow-up record for interface-boundary decisions.

devbot: incident-bot: note added to "model-rotation" runbook
